lit: when it comes to telling it, the words are long

use.how: Said before or instead of an explanation whose background takes long to tell: 这事说来话长。 Often a gentle way to put the story off.

near.diff: 一言难尽 says it can't be summed up briefly, often because it was hard or bitter; 说来话长 only says the story is long.

cue: A friend asks why you moved to another city. The reason involves years of events, and you would rather tell it over dinner later.

ctx.s: “你们俩是怎么认识的？”“{说来话长}，我们是在火车上认识的。”
ctx.en: "How did you two meet?" "It's a long story. We met on a train."

ctx.s: 他叹了口气说：“这件事{说来话长}，等有空我再慢慢告诉你。”
ctx.en: He sighed: "It's a long story; I'll tell you properly when I have time."

ctx.s: 我为什么辞职？{说来话长}，咱们先点菜吧。
ctx.en: Why did I quit? It's a long story. Let's order first.

ctx.s: 这座老房子的来历{说来话长}，要从我爷爷那一代说起。
ctx.en: The history of this old house is a long story; it starts with my grandfather's generation.

ctx.s: 记者问她为什么回国，她只是笑着说：“{说来话长}。”
ctx.en: When the reporter asked why she had come back home, she just smiled and said, "It's a long story."

ctx.s: 说起这个品牌名字的由来，那可就{说来话长}了。
ctx.en: As for where this brand's name comes from, now that's a long story.

bad.s: 这部电影{说来话长}，我看了三个小时。
bad.en: (meant: this film is very long; I watched it for three hours)
bad.why: It is about a story that would take long to tell, not about something that is long in itself, such as a film or a meeting.

bad.s: 他每次开会都{说来话长}，大家都听烦了。
bad.en: (meant: he goes on and on at every meeting)
bad.why: It does not mean long-winded. It introduces a story that would take long to tell, not a person who talks too much.

mean: to tell the plain truth, frankly

use.how: Used intransitively as a predicate or as an opener before a frank, often unwelcome remark: 我就实话实说了。 跟你实话实说吧。

near.diff: 开门见山 is about getting to the point without preamble; 实话实说 is about saying the true thing even when it is unwelcome.

cue: Your friend asks what you honestly think of her new haircut. You don't like it, and you decide to tell her so instead of being polite.

ctx.s: 你问我觉得怎么样，那我就{实话实说}了：这道菜太咸。
ctx.en: Since you ask what I think, I'll be honest: this dish is too salty.

ctx.s: 跟你{实话实说}吧，这个月我真的没钱了。
ctx.en: To tell you the truth, I'm really out of money this month.

ctx.s: 医生，请您{实话实说}，我的病到底严不严重？
ctx.en: Doctor, please be frank with me. How serious is my illness, really?

ctx.s: 面试时被问到缺点，她{实话实说}，承认自己不太会安排时间。
ctx.en: Asked about her weaknesses in the interview, she told the plain truth and admitted she is not good at managing her time.

ctx.s: 他因为{实话实说}得罪了领导，可同事们心里都佩服他。
ctx.en: He offended his boss by speaking frankly, but his colleagues privately admired him.

ctx.s: “你是不是不喜欢我送的礼物？”“{实话实说}，这个颜色我不太喜欢。”
ctx.en: "You don't like the present I gave you, do you?" "Honestly, I'm not keen on the colour."

bad.s: 这本书{实话实说}地记录了那段历史。
bad.en: (meant: this book faithfully records that period of history)
bad.why: It describes a person speaking frankly to someone, not a book or record being accurate.

bad.s: 他把这件事{实话实说}给了妈妈。
bad.en: (meant: he told his mother the truth about it)
bad.why: It takes no object and cannot be followed by gei. Put the listener before it instead: gen mama shihua shishuo.

use.how: Usually an adverbial before a speech verb: 大家七嘴八舌地讨论起来。 Needs a group of people, each saying something different.

near.diff: 议论纷纷 is many people commenting or gossiping about something; 七嘴八舌 stresses many voices talking over each other at the same moment.

cue: The waiter asks a table of eight what they would like, and everyone starts calling out different orders at the same time.

ctx.s: 老师刚说完，同学们就{七嘴八舌}地讨论起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher finished, the students all started discussing it at once.

ctx.s: 你们别{七嘴八舌}的，一个一个说！
ctx.en: Don't all talk at once. One at a time!

ctx.s: 记者们围着球员，{七嘴八舌}地提问。
ctx.en: The reporters crowded round the player, all firing questions at once.

ctx.s: 家里人{七嘴八舌}地给我出主意，我反而更不知道怎么办了。
ctx.en: My whole family chimed in with advice all at once, and I ended up even less sure what to do.

ctx.s: 群里大家{七嘴八舌}，半天也没定下来去哪儿吃饭。
ctx.en: Everyone in the group chat had something to say, and after ages we still hadn't decided where to eat.

ctx.s: 会上大家{七嘴八舌}，主持人只好敲了敲桌子。
ctx.en: Everyone at the meeting was talking over each other, so the chair had to rap on the table.

bad.s: 我妹妹特别{七嘴八舌}，一个人能说一下午。
bad.en: (meant: my sister is very chatty; she can talk all afternoon)
bad.why: It needs a group of people talking at once. It cannot describe one talkative person.

bad.s: 全班同学{七嘴八舌}地回答：“明白了！”
bad.en: (meant: the whole class answered together, "Got it!")
bad.why: It means many different voices at once. A whole class saying the same words together needs yi kou tong sheng.

mean: to come straight to the point
lit: open the door and see the mountain

story.text: The phrase began as a term of literary criticism. The Southern Song critic Yan Yu wrote that Li Bai's opening lines were 'open the door and see the mountain': his poems show their subject from the very first line, with no lead-in. Later it came to describe any speech or writing that gets to the point at once.

use.how: Used as a predicate or adverbial about speaking or writing: 我就开门见山了。 他开门见山地问。 文章开门见山。

near.diff: 拐弯抹角 is the opposite: talking around the point instead of stating it.
直截了当 is directness in general, also in refusing or acting; 开门见山 is about raising the main point first.

cue: You meet a busy client for the first time. With ten minutes before their flight, you skip the small talk and state your proposal in your first sentence.

ctx.s: 时间不多，我就{开门见山}了：这个项目需要再加两个人。
ctx.en: We don't have much time, so I'll get straight to it: this project needs two more people.

ctx.s: 他一坐下就{开门见山}地问：“你打算什么时候还钱？”
ctx.en: The moment he sat down he asked outright: "When are you going to pay me back?"

ctx.s: 这篇文章{开门见山}，第一句就提出了作者的观点。
ctx.en: This article gets straight to the point; the very first sentence states the author's view.

ctx.s: 写求职信最好{开门见山}，先说明你申请的是哪个职位。
ctx.en: In a cover letter it's best to be direct and say first which position you are applying for.

ctx.s: 王经理说话一向{开门见山}，从来不绕弯子。
ctx.en: Manager Wang always gets straight to the point and never beats about the bush.

ctx.s: 别铺垫那么多了，{开门见山}地说吧，你到底想让我帮什么忙？
ctx.en: Enough of the lead-up. Get to the point: what exactly do you want me to help with?

bad.s: 我一打开窗户就{开门见山}，风景真美。
bad.en: (meant: as soon as I opened the window I saw the mountains)
bad.why: It is only used figuratively, about speaking or writing; it never describes a real view.

bad.s: 他{开门见山}地把房子卖了。
bad.en: (meant: he sold the house without hesitating)
bad.why: It is about raising the main point in speech or writing, not about doing something decisively.

lit: to turn the bends and skirt round the corners

use.how: Mostly an adverbial or predicate about roundabout talk: 别拐弯抹角了。 他拐弯抹角地问。 Can also describe a winding route.

near.diff: 开门见山 is the opposite: raising the main point at once.
吞吞吐吐 is halting, hesitant speech; 拐弯抹角 can be fluent but avoids the point.

cue: Your roommate talks for ten minutes about rising prices and his tough job, and only at the very end hints that he'd like to borrow some money.

ctx.s: 有话直说，别{拐弯抹角}的。
ctx.en: Say what you mean. Stop beating around the bush.

ctx.s: 他{拐弯抹角}地问了半天，原来是想借我的车。
ctx.en: He hinted around for ages, and it turned out he wanted to borrow my car.

ctx.s: 她不好意思直接拒绝，就{拐弯抹角}地说自己最近太忙。
ctx.en: She was too embarrassed to refuse outright, so she said in a roundabout way that she'd been very busy lately.

ctx.s: 你{拐弯抹角}说了这么多，到底想要什么？
ctx.en: You've gone round in circles for so long. What is it you actually want?

ctx.s: 批评下属的时候，他总是{拐弯抹角}，结果对方根本没听懂。
ctx.en: When he criticises his staff he always talks around it, so the person never gets the message.

ctx.s: 出租车在老城的小巷里{拐弯抹角}，开了很久才到。
ctx.en: The taxi wound its way through the old town's alleys and took ages to get there.

bad.s: 这个问题很复杂，他{拐弯抹角}地解释得非常清楚。
bad.en: (meant: he explained this complex issue very clearly, from every angle)
bad.why: It criticises avoiding the point, so it cannot go with praise for a clear explanation.

bad.s: 他太{拐弯抹角}了，到现在还没决定。
bad.en: (meant: he is so indecisive that he still hasn't decided)
bad.why: It is about roundabout talk or a winding route, not about being unable to make up one's mind.

use.how: A noun phrase, usually an object: 说甜言蜜语, 被甜言蜜语骗了. Implies words meant to please or win someone over, often insincere; between lovers it can be light.

near.diff: 花言巧语 is clever, deceptive talk used to trick someone; 甜言蜜语 is flattering, affectionate talk that may or may not be sincere.

cue: Every time your friend's boyfriend forgets something important, he makes up for it with a flood of compliments and promises he never keeps.

ctx.s: 他就会说{甜言蜜语}，真到需要帮忙的时候人就不见了。
ctx.en: All he's good at is sweet talk; when you actually need help, he's nowhere to be found.

ctx.s: 别被推销员的{甜言蜜语}骗了，先看看合同。
ctx.en: Don't be taken in by the salesman's sweet talk; read the contract first.

ctx.s: 刚谈恋爱的时候，他每天都对我说{甜言蜜语}。
ctx.en: When we first started dating, he said sweet things to me every day.

ctx.s: 妈妈提醒她：“光听{甜言蜜语}没用，要看他怎么做。”
ctx.en: Her mother warned her: "Sweet words mean nothing; watch what he does."

ctx.s: 这些{甜言蜜语}我早就听腻了，你还是说点实在的吧。
ctx.en: I'm sick of all this honeyed talk. Tell me something real.

ctx.s: 故事里的骗子靠着{甜言蜜语}，骗走了老人一辈子的积蓄。
ctx.en: In the story, the con man used sweet talk to cheat the old man out of his life savings.

bad.s: 老师的{甜言蜜语}让我很感动，我决定更加努力。
bad.en: (meant: my teacher's kind encouragement moved me, so I decided to work harder)
bad.why: It suggests flattery meant to win someone over, often insincere, so it cannot describe a teacher's sincere encouragement.

bad.s: 这家店的蛋糕真是{甜言蜜语}。
bad.en: (meant: this shop's cakes are really sweet)
bad.why: It is only about words, never about taste.

mean: to say the same thing in unison

use.how: An adverbial before a speech verb: 大家异口同声地说。 Also used when everyone asked gives the same answer or opinion.

near.diff: 不约而同 is any action people happen to do together without arranging it; 异口同声 is only about saying the same thing.
七嘴八舌 is many people saying different things at once; 异口同声 is many saying the same thing.

cue: You ask three children whether they want to go to the zoo, and all three shout "Yes!" at exactly the same moment.

ctx.s: 老师问：“作业写完了吗？”同学们{异口同声}地说：“写完了！”
ctx.en: The teacher asked, "Have you finished your homework?" and the class answered in chorus, "Yes!"

ctx.s: 我问两个孩子想吃什么，他们{异口同声}地喊：“冰淇淋！”
ctx.en: I asked the two kids what they wanted to eat, and they both shouted, "Ice cream!"

ctx.s: 双胞胎{异口同声}地叫了一声“爸爸”，把他逗笑了。
ctx.en: The twins said "Daddy!" in perfect unison, which made him laugh.

ctx.s: 问起这家餐厅，几位老顾客{异口同声}地说好。
ctx.en: When asked about this restaurant, the regulars all said the same thing: it's good.

ctx.s: 对于这个方案，评委们几乎{异口同声}地表示反对。
ctx.en: The judges objected to the plan almost with one voice.

ctx.s: 被问到谁最努力，队员们{异口同声}地喊出了队长的名字。
ctx.en: Asked who worked hardest, the players all called out the captain's name together.

bad.s: 我和朋友{异口同声}地穿了一样的衣服。
bad.en: (meant: my friend and I happened to wear the same clothes)
bad.why: It is only about speaking. Happening to wear the same clothes without arranging it is bu yue er tong.

bad.s: 大家{异口同声}地发表了不同的意见。
bad.en: (meant: everyone voiced different opinions at once)
bad.why: It means saying the same thing, so it contradicts different opinions. Many different voices at once is qi zui ba she.

mean: to do the same thing without having agreed to
lit: without arranging it, and yet the same

use.how: An adverbial before a verb, with two or more people as subject: 我们不约而同地笑了。 Stresses that the shared action was not planned.

near.diff: 异口同声 is only saying the same words; 不约而同 covers any action or reaction people happen to share.
不谋而合 is ideas or plans turning out to match; 不约而同 is mostly people doing the same thing at the same time.

cue: Without texting each other, you and your sister both turn up at your parents' house on the same evening, each with a cake.

ctx.s: 听到这个消息，我们{不约而同}地笑了起来。
ctx.en: When we heard the news, we all burst out laughing at the same time.

ctx.s: 聚会那天，我和她{不约而同}地穿了红裙子。
ctx.en: On the day of the party, she and I both happened to wear red dresses.

ctx.s: 你们俩是商量好的吗？怎么{不约而同}地选了同一个题目？
ctx.en: Did you two plan this? How did you both pick the same topic?

ctx.s: 两位作家{不约而同}地把故事放在了同一个小镇。
ctx.en: Independently of each other, the two writers set their stories in the same small town.

ctx.s: 停电以后，邻居们{不约而同}地走到楼下，互相打听情况。
ctx.en: After the power cut, the neighbours all came downstairs of their own accord to ask each other what was going on.

ctx.s: 那年春节，兄弟三人{不约而同}地回到了老家。
ctx.en: That Spring Festival, the three brothers all went back to their hometown without arranging it.

bad.s: 我们提前约好了，所以{不约而同}地在门口见面。
bad.en: (meant: we had arranged it, so we met at the door)
bad.why: It means without having arranged it, so it contradicts the first half: we had arranged it in advance.

bad.s: 他俩的性格{不约而同}，都很安静。
bad.en: (meant: their personalities are alike; both are quiet)
bad.why: It describes people happening to act alike at one moment, not a lasting likeness such as similar personalities.

use.how: Usually after 从, 向 or 来自, about people or things moving from or to every side: 从四面八方赶来, 向四面八方散去.

near.diff: 五湖四海 is about people coming from all over the country or world; 四面八方 is any movement from or to every direction, near or far.

cue: A whistle blows in the park, and dogs come running back to their owners from every side.

ctx.s: 烟花一响，孩子们从{四面八方}跑了过来。
ctx.en: When the fireworks went off, children came running from every direction.

ctx.s: 鸽子被吓了一跳，向{四面八方}飞去。
ctx.en: Startled, the pigeons flew off in all directions.

ctx.s: 站在山顶往{四面八方}看，全是一片绿色。
ctx.en: From the top of the mountain, everything you see in every direction is green.

ctx.s: 地震发生后，救援人员从{四面八方}赶到灾区。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, rescuers rushed to the disaster area from all sides.

ctx.s: 我们班的同学来自{四面八方}，口音都不一样。
ctx.en: The students in our class come from all over, and they all have different accents.

ctx.s: 音乐节还没开始，从{四面八方}来的歌迷就挤满了公园。
ctx.en: Before the music festival had even started, fans from all around had packed the park.

bad.s: 这家超市的东西{四面八方}，什么都有。
bad.en: (meant: this supermarket has all kinds of things)
bad.why: It is about directions and places, not about a shop offering a wide variety of goods.

bad.s: 他{四面八方}地考虑了这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: he considered the problem from every angle)
bad.why: It means directions in space. It cannot describe thinking about a problem from every angle.

lit: reaching the thousands, climbing to the ten-thousands

use.how: A number phrase before a countable noun, with 的 or a measure word: 成千上万的游客, 成千上万只鸟. Used for people, animals and repeated events.

near.diff: 人山人海 paints a scene packed with people; 成千上万 states a huge number of any countable thing.

cue: After one famous singer shared the charity's page, donations poured in from people beyond counting: not dozens, not hundreds, far more.

ctx.s: 每年春天，{成千上万}的游客来这里看樱花。
ctx.en: Every spring, tens of thousands of tourists come here to see the cherry blossoms.

ctx.s: 这个视频一发出去，就有{成千上万}的人点赞。
ctx.en: As soon as the video was posted, thousands upon thousands of people liked it.

ctx.s: 你知道吗？一个蜂巢里住着{成千上万}只蜜蜂。
ctx.en: Did you know a single hive is home to tens of thousands of bees?

ctx.s: 一到冬天，{成千上万}只候鸟飞到这片湖上过冬。
ctx.en: Every winter, vast numbers of migratory birds fly to this lake to spend the season.

ctx.s: 为了这个产品，工程师们做了{成千上万}次实验。
ctx.en: The engineers ran thousands upon thousands of tests for this product.

ctx.s: 这场洪水让{成千上万}的家庭失去了房子。
ctx.en: The flood left tens of thousands of families without homes.

bad.s: 我花了{成千上万}的时间学中文。
bad.en: (meant: I've spent a huge amount of time learning Chinese)
bad.why: It counts separate things such as people, animals or attempts. It cannot measure an amount of time.

bad.s: 广场上{成千上万}，挤得走不动。
bad.en: (meant: the square was so packed you couldn't move)
bad.why: It is a number phrase and needs a noun after it, such as people. A packed scene on its own is ren shan ren hai.
